questions.question: What is the first safety question for a patient with pelvic pain or abnormal bleeding and reproductive potential?
choices: What is the patient’s favorite contraceptive method
questions.explanation: Pregnancy status changes the differential, imaging pathway, medication safety, and urgency. Pregnancy-related emergencies must be considered early.

questions.question: Why can chronic anovulation cause irregular bleeding and increase endometrial risk?
choices: Progesterone exposure is prolonged every month
Inadequate cyclic progesterone allows prolonged estrogenic stimulation
questions.explanation: With ovulatory dysfunction, cyclic progesterone exposure may be inadequate. Prolonged estrogenic stimulation can produce irregular bleeding and endometrial effects.

questions.question: A patient has a positive pregnancy test, unilateral pelvic pain, light bleeding, dizziness, HR 112, and BP 90/58. What is the priority?
choices: Emergency evaluation for possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy
questions.explanation: Pregnancy plus pain, bleeding, and hemodynamic instability raises concern for ruptured ectopic pregnancy and internal hemorrhage; emergency transfer is required.

questions.question: Which presentation is most concerning for ovarian torsion?
choices: Sudden unilateral pelvic pain with nausea/vomiting
questions.explanation: Ovarian torsion commonly presents with acute unilateral pelvic pain and nausea/vomiting. Delayed evaluation can threaten ovarian viability.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects PID clinical reasoning?
choices: One laboratory test always confirms PID
PID is only present with high fever
PID may be subtle; delayed recognition can contribute to infertility and ectopic-pregnancy risk
questions.explanation: PID is a clinical diagnosis with variable findings. Delayed diagnosis/treatment can contribute to tubal damage, chronic pain, infertility, and ectopic-pregnancy risk.

questions.question: A patient has lower abdominal pain, new discharge, cervical motion tenderness, and adnexal tenderness. What is an appropriate FNP concern?
choices: Possible PID while also considering surgical and pregnancy-related emergencies
A benign condition that never needs follow-up
questions.explanation: This pattern can be compatible with PID. The FNP also assesses pregnancy status, severity, and alternate emergencies such as ectopic pregnancy, torsion, or appendicitis.

questions.question: Which finding should prompt diagnostic evaluation rather than reassurance that symptoms are only menopausal?
questions.explanation: New postmenopausal bleeding requires prompt evaluation for endometrial and other pathology; it should not be presumed hormonal.

questions.question: What is a core mechanism linking PCOS to endometrial risk?
choices: Chronic anovulation with prolonged estrogenic stimulation
Reduced androgen activity in all patients
questions.explanation: Ovulatory dysfunction can result in insufficient cyclic progesterone exposure and prolonged estrogenic stimulation of the endometrium.

questions.question: A patient with heavy uterine bleeding has syncope, dyspnea, and lightheadedness. What is the safest disposition?
choices: Emergency evaluation for possible hemodynamic compromise or symptomatic anemia
questions.explanation: Heavy ongoing bleeding with syncope, dyspnea, or symptomatic anemia can be an emergency and needs immediate evaluation.

questions.question: Which approach best reflects FNP-level pelvic-pain assessment?
choices: Name one gynecologic diagnosis before obtaining pregnancy status
Assess stability, pregnancy status, time course, focused differential, and emergency red flags
Assume all pelvic pain is PID
Order the same test panel for every patient
questions.explanation: Safe assessment integrates hemodynamics, pregnancy status, symptom trajectory, targeted examination/testing, alternatives, and early escalation for emergencies.
